claims: The current La Niña is fading.
A transition to ENSO-neutral is expected in the next month.
The transition to ENSO-neutral is expected to last through May-July 2026.
The Climate Prediction Center's 2026 report indicates a 62% chance of El Niño forming by June-August 2026.
The Climate Prediction Center's 2026 report indicates a high likelihood of El Niño lasting through the end of the year.
There is a significant 1-in-3 chance that the El Niño event could be "strong" during the October-December 2026 period.
According to AccuWeather, a developing El Niño could bring higher wind shear to the Atlantic Basin.
According to AccuWeather, a developing El Niño could potentially act as a "roadblock" to a hyperactive hurricane season.
The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) and NOAA warn that spring forecasts are less reliable.
Current subsurface ocean heat strongly suggests the transition to ENSO-neutral.
